html:
SMTO-CTX-0042 — SMTO asked for a part of a saved result that isn't there

GUID: de8b1e7c-0f54-5029-8cad-3f90bf5fbae0
Slug: task-context-pointer-invalid
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: task-context

What happened

  • SMTO looked inside a saved result from this Task for a specific piece, such as a command's output, and that piece doesn't exist in it. Nothing in your conversation was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the Task is still running, wait for it. SMTO normally looks at the saved result and picks a part that exists. The error gives SMTO a list of the parts it can read, so it doesn't need to guess again.
  2. If the Task has stopped, select Continue task, or send a short message in the same conversation such as "Please continue". A new step lets SMTO read the saved result again using a part that is actually there.
  3. If SMTO keeps asking for a command's separate output or error text, tell it in the conversation to read the whole saved output instead. Some saved command results keep all output together, so a separate error-only part doesn't exist.

What success looks like

  • The Task moves past this step and SMTO quotes or summarizes the saved result it was looking for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't run the earlier command again just to recreate the output; the saved result still exists, only the requested part is missing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Task Context read used a JSON Pointer that is malformed or absent in the source (invalid_or_missing_pointer), or requested an operation-receipt field the receipt does not provide (field_unavailable).

What this means

  • The source does not expose the requested JSON field or pointer. The recorded reason and operation message identify the specific condition.

Why this can happen

  • The source exists but the requested JSON Pointer is malformed or absent.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation, reason, revision and source reference recorded by the producer.

How to fix it

  • For invalid_or_missing_pointer, read a small page of the same reference without pointer or cursor (the returned next_action caps max_characters at 1000) and pick a pointer that actually exists. For field_unavailable, choose one of the returned available_pointers; combined output is not a separate /stdout stream. Do not guess field names or bypass access and revision checks.
  • Read a small page without pointer to inspect the source, then use an observed available pointer.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the indicated argument or refresh the source first; retain existing access checks and revision checks.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected notebook operation succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass source access checks or overwrite a revision conflict.

Technical notes

  • An unavailable source does not prove that no relevant information exists.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-CTX-0028 — SMTO couldn't find an item in this Task's saved notes
